correctness.rationale: For the repaired finding, adjacency implies |d(w,u)−d(w,v)|≤1. The integer difference is nonzero precisely when it is ±1, in which case appending the edge to the shorter geodesic gives the required geodesic containing the nearer endpoint. The strong condition implies the same ±1 equality by splitting the geodesic. This identifies each constraint and thus every feasible and optimal function, including for the empty constraint family. For a graph with an edge, a constraint gives the lower bound 1. Bipartition makes distances to adjacent endpoints opposite in parity, so concentration of weight 1 at any vertex attains it. Conversely a weight-one minimizer must have every positive-weight vertex in every resolving neighborhood; the parity of distance from such a vertex is a proper two-coloring. The minimizer exists by compactness and nonemptiness. The K1 zero minimum and C4 value one follow directly. The frozen enumerator excludes order 1 and is not evidence for the removed overclaim; no uploaded code was executed.
residual_risks: The proof uses unweighted integer edge distances and adjacency. It does not identify the all-pairs strong and ordinary parameters.

originality.rationale: The surviving contribution is an exact identification of a separately introduced adjacent-pair LP, together with a correction of a stated general characterization. The ordinary bipartite characterization is prior, and K1 is a scope repair, not new mathematics. The equality is a short consequence of the published definitions, but the introducing paper explicitly gives only a one-sided comparison and draws an incompatible path-only conclusion. The comparison concerns whether the identification and correction are already established, not whether they are hard to derive.
